item.title: 40 beggars, vagrants held near Dhaka airport
item.description:
By FE ONLINE REPORT

Bangladesh has expressed interest in joining the Mecca Joint Defence Pact signed this month by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, the country’s foreign affairs state minister, Humaiun Kobir, said on Monday.

“We have expressed our interest in the Mecca Joint Defence Pact. Bangladesh recognises it, and there is an interest,” Kobir told reporters at the foreign ministry in Dhaka.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the defence agreement in Mecca on 7 August, establishing a framework for closer security and defence cooperation among the three countries.

Kobir said Bangladesh’s interest in such an arrangement should not be viewed as unusual, given the country’s close ties with Saudi Arabia and the wider Muslim world.

“Mecca has always held a special place,” he said. “Mecca is in the hearts of Bangladesh and its people. If a security alliance is formed among countries in the Middle East or the Islamic world, it would not be unusual for Bangladesh to join.”

His comments come as the government seeks to strengthen Bangladesh’s engagement with Muslim-majority countries while pursuing a broader foreign policy centred on strategic partnerships.

Kobir also said Bangladesh and India were working together to finalise the dates for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s proposed visit to New Delhi.

“The two countries are working on this. The dates will be finalised through discussions at a mutually convenient time for Dhaka and Delhi,” he said.

The visit would be closely watched amid efforts by the two neighbours to recalibrate their relationship and address outstanding bilateral issues through high-level political engagement.

Asked about questions surrounding his British citizenship and whether he had relinquished it before taking office, Kobir thrashed the idea, saying that he is a Bangladeshi citizen and those who are accusing him of having dual citizenship are against the interest of Bangladesh.

“I am Bangladeshi,” he said. “The very fact that I have come here and am working for Bangladesh means that.”

item.title: 40 beggars, vagrants held near Dhaka airport
item.description:
Police on Monday arrested 40 beggars and vagrants at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in the capital.

The Airport Police Station conducted the drive at the airport roundabout, BRTA station, Airport Railway Station, areas around police boxes, airport entrances and VIP Road, said Additional Deputy Commissioner (Media) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police Niaz Mehedi.

Police said the presence of beggars and vagrants in the airport area had long been causing inconvenience to local and foreign passengers, reports UNB.

Of those arrested, 15 were children, two were women, and 23 were adult men.

Police said steps were being taken to send the children to the Training and Rehabilitation Centre for the Vagrant in Mirpur, while the adults will be produced before a special court.

Airport police said around 288 more beggars and vagrants had been arrested in similar drives over the past several days.

With Monday’s arrests, the total number of people arrested so far stands at 328, police said.

Police said the detained children were sent to the Training and Rehabilitation Centre for the Vagrant in Mirpur, while the adults were sent to jail through the special court process.

The drives will continue to ensure the smooth movement of passengers and overall security in and around the airport area, police said.

item.title: Ex-home minister Mohabbat Jan dies
item.description:
By bdnews24.com

Former home minister Mohabbat Jan Chowdhury, who served under former military ruler HM Ershad, has died at the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) at the age of 92.

Mohammad Abdul Hoque, chairman of the Retired Armed Forces Officers Welfare Association (RAOWA) Club, confirmed his death on Monday.

He is scheduled to be buried at the military cemetery after funeral prayers following Maghrib in Uttara Sector 4.

Chowdhury joined the Pakistan Army as a second lieutenant in 1955 and retired as a major general. He also served as director general of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI).

After Ershad seized power, Chowdhury was appointed home minister in 1982, serving from July that year until July 1983.

Born in Gopalganj subdivision of Faridpur district, he later entered politics and won the Faridpur-3 seat in the 1986 election on a Jatiya Party ticket.

He also served as a director on the board of Micro Industries Development Assistance and Services.

item.title: Govt to launch post-accident emergency service on highways
item.description:
By FE ONLINE REPORT

FE Online

The government will soon roll out a post-accident emergency service on highways through 60 basic life-support ambulances, 40 motorcycle ambulances and 80 highway patrol motorcycles by providing post-crash medical services and highway patrol operations with the aim of halving road fatalities.

Under the project, 60 basic life-support ambulances will be deployed at 10-kilometre intervals along the Joydebpur–Hatikamrul–Bogura–Rangpur, Hatikamrul–Natore–Rajshahi and Joydebpur–Mymensingh national highways.

Under the multi-agency project -- Bangladesh Road Safety Project,-- the emergency vehicles will operate within 500-kilometer areas, supported by trained medical assistants and volunteers.

A ceremony in this connection was held at the Roads and Highways Department (RHD) conference room on Monday.

Road Transport and Bridges, Railways and Shipping Minister Sheikh Robiul Alam attended the event as the chief guest and said road accidents and resulting fatalities can be reduced by a half by 2030 if drivers and pedestrians are made more aware, effective enforcement of laws is ensured, and emergency medical services are provided promptly.

State Minister for Road Transport and Bridges and Railways Habibur Rashid, who attended as the special guest, said the programme marks a milestone in ensuring road safety.

He added that arrangements have been made to ensure that ambulances reach accident sites as quickly as possible so that speeding vehicles never bring human lives to a halt.

Project Director Sabbir Hasan Khan Ahmed said that operations for the post-accident emergency service will officially commence by September, with a joint venture operator providing the service for two years.

He noted that the vehicles will be available and monitored 24/7.

item.title: Measles: 5 more die as suspected caseload tops 150,000
item.description:
By bdnews24.com

Five more people with measles symptoms have died in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

Three of them were recorded in the Dhaka Division, with the other two in the Sylhet and Chattogram divisions.

The number of suspected cases of the highly-contagious disease has also risen to 150,652.

Since Mar 15, 839 people with measles symptoms have died nationwide, while measles was confirmed in 99 other deaths, according to the health directorate.

The DGHS bulletin on Sunday said 83 people tested positive for measles in the 24 hours until 8am on Monday.

Dhaka Division has recorded the highest number of deaths with measles symptoms at 372, followed by Sylhet with 141. Rajshahi recorded 92 deaths, Mymensingh 74, Chattogram 64, Barishal 49, Khulna 33, and Rangpur 14.

Over the past 24 hours, 1,149 people sought hospital care with measles symptoms, with 1,055 admitted.

Of the new admissions, 319 were in Dhaka Division, 31 in Rajshahi, nine in Sylhet, 307 in Chattogram, 154 in Barishal, 53 in Mymensingh, 73 in Khulna, and 20 in Rangpur.

With these admissions, the number of measles patients hospitalised nationwide has reached 131,609. Of them, 126,921 have been discharged after treatment, according to the DGHS.

A total of 18,487 cases have been confirmed, the DGHS said.

item.title: China-Bangladesh ties pass global test: Xi
item.description:
By bdnews24.com

In a congratulatory message to Bangladesh’s new head of state Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, Chinese President Xi Jinping has said Beijing and Dhaka have weathered shifting global currents.

Xi sent the message on Monday, a day after Fakhrul took office as Bangladesh’s 23rd president, according to a statement posted by the Chinese Embassy in Dhaka.

“China-Bangladesh bilateral relationship has withstood the test of changing international circumstances,” Xi wrote.

He described China and Bangladesh as neighbours with a longstanding friendship, saying the two countries had respected and treated each other as equals over the 51 years since establishing diplomatic ties.

They have also supported each other on issues involving their core interests and major concerns while pursuing their respective paths to modernisation hand in hand, he said.

Xi said he was ready to work with Fakhrul to “carry forward traditional friendship, strengthen strategic communications, enhance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, and expand cooperation exchanges in all sectors”.

The efforts, he said, would help deepen the “China-Bangladesh community with a shared future in the new era” and steadily deliver tangible benefits for both peoples.

Fakhrul took oath on Friday evening as the country’s new president, after stepping down as local government minister and secretary general of the ruling BNP to assume the presidency.

item.title: Nusrat murder: Mother satisfied with HC verdict
item.description:
By FE ONLINE DESK

Shirin Akter, the mother of madrasah student Nusrat Jahan Rafi, has expressed satisfaction with the High Court (HC) verdict in the widely discussed case over the murder of her daughter.

She also sought security for her family, alleging that they have received arson threats.

Shirin Akter was talking to the media at her house in the Char Chandia area of Sonagazi upazila of Feni on Monday, following the verdict, according to media reports.

She said, “Many people tried to term Nusrat murder suicide after the incident. However, with the verdict today, it has been proved once again that it was a murder. I am satisfied, Alhamdulillah.”

She further said, “We are being threatened that our homes will be set on fire. We seek security for our family from the Prime Minister and the authorities concerned.”

A High Court bench comprising Justice Bhishmadev Chakraborty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja on Monday upheld the death sentences for two convicts in the Nusrat murder case after hearing death references, appeals and jail appeals filed in the case.

The two convicts are Siraj Ud Daula, expelled principal of Sonagazi Islamia Fazil (Degree) Madrasah, and Shahadat Hossain Shamim. Besides, the court commuted death penalty for four other convicts to life imprisonment and acquitted 10 others.

The life imprisonment awardees are Umme Sultana Popi, Mohammad Nuruddin, shahadat Hossain Jabed and Iftekhar Hossain Rana.

Relatives of both the victim and convicts were present at the court during the verdict.

According to the prosecution, Siraj Ud Daula sexually harassed Nusrat in his office on March 27, 2019. He was arrested after a case was filed over the incident.

According to the case document, on April 6 in 2019, Nusrat was taken to the roof of the madrasah building after she refused to withdraw the case against the principal. Her hands and legs were tied, and kerosene was poured over her before she was set on fire.

Nusrat succumbed to injuries on April 10 while undergoing treatment in the burn unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

item.title: Dengue admissions hit year-high as 3 more die
item.description:
By bdnews24.com

Bangladesh has recorded three more dengue deaths and 994 hospital admissions in a 24-hour count.

This is the highest number of fresh cases in a single day this year. Previously, the daily high was 805 on Aug 16 and 756 on Aug 11.

According to Monday’s bulletin from the Directorate General of Health Services, 97 patients were admitted to hospitals in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and 126 in Dhaka South over a 24-hour count.

Also, 148 cases were registered in the Dhaka Division outside of the two city corporations.

Among other divisions, 117 patients were admitted in Barishal, 107 in Chattogram, 215 in Khulna, 71 in Mymensingh, 76 in Rajshahi, 23 in Rangpur and four in Sylhet.

The health directorate says 85 people have died from the Aedes mosquito-borne disease this year. Of them 31 have died in August.

A total of 29,923 dengue patients have been hospitalised since Jan 1, with 27,758 discharged after treatment. Another 862 patients left hospitals in the latest 24-hour period.

The DGHS has tracked dengue hospitalisations and deaths since 2000. The highest toll came in 2023, when 321,179 patients were hospitalised and 1,705 died.

Last year, dengue killed more than 400 people, while around 102,000 cases were reported.

item.title: SSC exams to start in March, not January
item.description:
By bdnews24.com

The education administration has reversed its decision to start the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent exams from Jan 7 next year.

Taking into account the opinions of examinees and guardians, it has decided the exams will begin in March after the holy month of Ramadan and Eid-ul-Fitr.

Next year's SSC and equivalent exams will start on Mar 14, said Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, president of the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee.

The Dhaka Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board chairman told bdnews24.com on Monday, "It will start on the 14th of March and end on the 15th of April. The routine will be posted on the website shortly."

The holy month of Ramadan is likely to start in the second week of February next year.

Accordingly, Eid-ul-Fitr will be in the second week of March, after the end of Ramadan.

On May 14, Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced that next year's SSC and equivalent exams will start on Jan 7.

The announcement led to debate and criticism from educators, students, and guardians. The proposed schedule for the exam has already been published.

However, on Jun 2, while facing reporters at the Secretariat, the education minister said that if stakeholders want to push for a change to the schedule, the exams could be pushed back.

Students set to take their SSC exams next year have seen several disruptions to their education.

They studied the new curriculum formed by the Awami League from grades 6 to 8 before they were brought to the revised curriculum of 2010 in grades 9 and 10 according to the decision of the interim government.

The interim government also had issues getting textbooks to students on time.

Many examinees and their guardians felt that if the schedule were moved up to February, it would only pile onto the disruptions faced by the approximately 2 million students set to take the exams next year.

Although it was once customary for SSC and equivalent exams to be held in February and Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent exams in April, the schedule has been disrupted regularly since the COVID-19 pandemic and the July Uprising. Subsequently, the SSC and equivalent exams have started in April and HSC and equivalent exams in July.

Education Minister Milon had planned to readjust the SSC and equivalent exams to January to save time for students.

item.title: 20pc of coastal adults over 40 at heart risk, study finds
item.description:
By FE ONLINE REPORT

One in five adults aged 40 years or older in some coastal villages were found with cardiovascular disease risk, said a new study on Monday.

Of these, about one in five (21.6 per cent) were estimated to have a moderate-to-high 10-year risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), defined as a risk of at least 10 per cent, it added. .

The findings were presented at a high-level policy and dissemination seminar titled “Drinking Water Salinity and Impact on Health: Bangladesh Evidence and Policy Recommendations”, organised by icddr,b in collaboration with Imperial College London at icddr,b, headquarters in Dhaka city.

The research assessed the cardiovascular disease risk among 15,471 adults in Koyra and Assasuni.

The prevalence was 19.7 per cent in Koyra and 23.6 per cent in Assasuni, with both areas showing substantially higher levels than the national estimate of approximately 9.02 per cent.

The study was conducted from 2023-2025.

Senior Scientist at icddr,b Dr Aliya Naheed presented preliminary findings from the Bangladesh programme of the NIHR Global Health Research Centre for Non-Communicable Diseases and Environmental Change.

The programme first assessed drinking-water sources in 172 villages in 71 Community Clinic catchment areas in Koyra Upazila of Khulna, the intervention area, and Assasuni Upazila of Satkhira, the usual-care comparison area.

Researchers also surveyed 27,697 water sources, of which 6,703 (24.2 per cent) were being used for drinking. Among drinking-water sources, 55.3 per cent in Koyra and 23.3 per cent in Assasuni were found to contain saline.

Secretary In-Charge, Environment Ministry, Fahmida Khanom, addressed the event as the chief guest where she emphasised collaboration with government agencies and organisations like icddr,b and the universities to help the affected people with government interventions.

Blaming climate change for the increasing salinity problem in the coastal region, she said, “It gives Bangladesh stronger evidence to take to international climate negotiations and emphasises adaptation and mitigation strategy.”

Based on this evidence, the research team has designed a package of water and primary healthcare interventions integrating digital innovation.

Prof Paolo Vineis of Imperial College London stressed the need for national and international institutions to consider developing appropriate guidelines for health-based threshold for drinking water, while research continues to clarify how sodium and other minerals affect health.

Prof Adrian Butler of Imperial College London presented evidence on how tropical-cyclone storm surges can cause long-term salinisation of drinking-water ponds and shallow groundwater.

Dr Tahmeed Ahmed, Executive Director of icddr,b, said that evidence linking climate change with health outcomes in Bangladesh remains limited.

Md Lutfor Rahman, Director General, Department of Environment, Sheikh Momena Moni, Additional Secretary, Health Ministry spoke as the special guests while Pravath Chandra Biswas, Director General of the Directorate General of Health Services, chaired the event.
